Let \(x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)^T\). Updating coordinate \(i\) sets \((Ax)_i=0\), so
\[
x_1=-\frac{x_2+x_3}{2},\qquad
x_2=-\frac{x_1+x_3}{2},\qquad
x_3=-\frac{x_1+x_2}{3}.
\]

For a sweep order \(\pi\), write \(x^\pi=T_\pi x\). Then
\[
\frac{\mathbb E_q f(x^\pi)}{f(x)}
=\frac{x^T\left(\sum_\pi q_\pi T_\pi^TAT_\pi\right)x}{x^TAx}.
\]
Thus \(\rho(q)\) is the largest generalized eigenvalue of \(\sum q_\pi T_\pi^TAT_\pi\) relative to \(A\).

Because \(A\) is invariant under swapping coordinates \(1,2\), an optimal distribution may be symmetrized under this swap. So put total weights
\[
\alpha=q_{123}+q_{213},\qquad
\beta=q_{132}+q_{231},\qquad
\gamma=q_{312}+q_{321},
\]
with equal split inside each pair. Then \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1\). The averaged matrix \(B=\mathbb E(T_\pi^TAT_\pi)\) has form
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}
d&o&r\\
o&d&r\\
r&r&z
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

The antisymmetric line \((1,-1,0)\) gives the eigenvalue
\[
\lambda_-=d-o
=\frac{17}{96}\alpha+\frac{19}{72}\beta+\frac{3}{16}\gamma.
\]

On the symmetric plane \(x=(s,s,t)\),
\[
x^TAx=6s^2+4st+3t^2,
\]
while
\[
x^TBx=
\left(\frac{17}{48}\alpha+\frac{19}{36}\beta+\frac{91}{72}\gamma\right)s^2
+\left(\frac58\alpha+\frac{11}{18}\beta\right)st
+\left(\frac{11}{16}\alpha+\frac{13}{36}\beta\right)t^2.
\]

The optimum occurs with \(\beta=0\), and with the antisymmetric eigenvalue equal to the largest symmetric-plane eigenvalue. Put \(\gamma=1-\alpha\). Then
\[
\lambda_-=\frac{18-\alpha}{96}.
\]
The equality condition for the symmetric block is
\[
\det(S-\lambda_-D)=0,
\]
where
\[
S=
\begin{bmatrix}
\frac{182-131\alpha}{144}&\frac{5\alpha}{16}\\[2mm]
\frac{5\alpha}{16}&\frac{11\alpha}{16}
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
D=
\begin{bmatrix}
6&2\\
2&3
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Substitution gives
\[
(10-61\alpha)(23\alpha-18)-4(8\alpha-9)^2=0,
\]
or
\[
1659\alpha^2-1904\alpha+504=0.
\]
The relevant root is
\[
\alpha=\frac{952+2\sqrt{17542}}{1659}.
\]
Hence
\[
\rho_*=\frac{18-\alpha}{96}
=\frac{14455-\sqrt{17542}}{79632}.
\]

This value is attained, for example, by
\[
q_{123}=q_{213}=\frac{476+\sqrt{17542}}{1659},\qquad
q_{312}=q_{321}=\frac{707-2\sqrt{17542}}{3318},
\]
and
\[
q_{132}=q_{231}=0.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac{14455-\sqrt{17542}}{79632}}.
\]
